title: Instagram’s new tool for creators targets unauthorized reposts and AI-modified videos
slides: Can Instagram stop others profiting from your face?
A new tool detects reposts and AI-altered clips automatically
But detection only works if creators manually register their content first
Creators can now file bulk takedowns without chasing each video
Check if your profile is eligible before competitors repost you
thread_text:
1. Your Face, Their Profit?

Instagram now lets you detect reposts and AI-altered clips automatically — but some creators still get paid from your content. Here's how to fight back.

2. Detection Is Automatic

A new tool scans for reposts and AI manipulations of your videos. You don't have to hunt them down manually anymore.

3. Manual Registration Required

Detection only works if you register your content first. Without that step, the system can't match stolen clips to your profile.

4. Bulk Takedowns, One Request

Now you can file bulk takedowns without chasing each video individually. One form, multiple reports — saves hours of back-and-forth.

5. Is Your Profile Eligible?

Before competitors repost your work, check if your account qualifies for the tool. Open Instagram's help center and search "content protection" — do it today.

instagram.caption:
Someone can repost your video, run it through an AI filter, and collect the views while you get nothing. 🎯

Instagram's new tool now scans for reposts and AI-altered versions of your clips automatically, no manual hunting required.

But there's a catch: detection only kicks in if you register your content first. Skip that step, and the system can't match stolen clips to your profile.

Once you're in, you can file bulk takedowns in one request instead of chasing each video. 🔍

For anyone who posts original work, this means hours saved and fewer copycats slipping through. ⏱️

Open Instagram's help center, search "content protection," and check if your account qualifies — before someone else profits from your face. ✅
